A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. Before a stage I-III patient is judged too frail, they get an exercise test, a geriatric assessment if over 75, and four weeks of supervised exercise, breathing training and help to stop smoking. Then the decision is made again.
effect_summary_en: A Cochrane review (2022: 10 trials, 636 patients) found that exercise before lung cancer surgery cuts lung complications after it (risk ratio 0.45), but it did not measure how many more patients became fit for curative treatment.
supported_en: Cochrane 2022: exercise before surgery cuts lung complications after lung cancer surgery by more than half (RR 0.45) and shortens the hospital stay by about 2.2 days.
not_supported_en: No page read shows the assumed gain of 0.5 percentage points (range 0–1.5) in the share of patients treated with curative intent.
summary_en: Neither the OYS pages nor the Pohde pages read show any public sign of a fitness assessment and prehabilitation programme before curative treatment is ruled out. The OYS pathway page only says that lung function and other illnesses are weighed, and that just under a quarter of patients are suitable for surgery. A similar model exists at Tays in the Pirkanmaa region, not in Oulu. A 2022 Cochrane review shows exercise before surgery cuts lung complications (risk ratio 0.45), but it does not measure how many more patients become eligible for curative treatment.
unanswered_en: No page read says whether OYS has a prehabilitation or geriatric assessment route for lung cancer patients, and no study read measures how many more patients get curative-intent treatment.
